input.brief: Chemlife research platform pages: ANBioT, silk pupae green chelation, coated nutrient pearls, nano trace minerals and nature-identical molecules; interactive scientific diagrams, proprietary process and existing company photography

direction.name: The well-kept board
direction.idea: The whole page is a board of tiles fitted edge to edge with narrow gaps, like a tidy desk seen from above. Each tile is one thing: the name, a statement, a photograph, a number, a link, a short list. There is no hero and no sequence of bands; the page is one continuous composition that the eye roams. It suits subjects with many small true things to show (a studio with work, writing, clients and news; a product with several distinct capabilities) and it replaces the generic bento by having real content in every tile and a strict system for sizes.
direction.composition: A 12-column grid with 8px gaps and 8–12px outer margins, filled completely, no empty cells. Tiles use only four sizes (for example 6×4, 6×2, 3×2, 3×4 in column × row units of about 90px). Every tile is a flat filled rectangle: ground colour one step from the page, or a palette colour, or a photograph covering it. One radius everywhere (0, or 6–10px). The first screen contains: a name tile (the name at display size, the largest type on the page) with the wordmark set large, a statement tile with the description at 28–40px, two or three image tiles and one action tile in the accent colour. Text inside tiles is top-left aligned with 20–24px padding and never centred. Below the first screen the board continues with the same sizes; the last row is the footer made of tiles.
direction.typography: One grotesk in two weights. Inside tiles: a large size for single statements, a small size for lists. No uppercase labels in tile corners.
direction.colour: Page ground, tile ground one step lighter or darker, and one or two palette colours on selected tiles. Photographs supply the rest.
direction.imagery: Photographs fill whole tiles with `object-fit: cover`; choose images that crop well to both wide and tall tiles.
direction.richness: The fit. A full board with consistent gaps and varied tile contents is satisfying in the way a packed suitcase is.
direction.pitfalls: Tiles are filled, never outlined, and never carry shadows. Do not put an icon and a two-line feature blurb in every tile; vary what tiles hold. Decide the phone layout as its own board: two columns, tiles re-ordered so the name and statement lead.

hero.name: Sheet with a text cell
hero.blueprint: The whole viewport is a sheet of photographs: six columns with 12px gaps and 12px outer margins, each column a vertical stack of frames at natural ratios with square corners. Each column starts at a different vertical offset (0, -90, -40, -130, -20, -70px) so rows never line up and the top and bottom frames are cropped by the viewport. Every frame has a flat strip 28px tall fused to its bottom edge in a solid palette colour, carrying one line of 13px text (a title or a place); strip colours rotate through four values. There is no header. In columns 3-4, starting at 28% of the height, one cell of the sheet is not a photograph but a filled panel in the tone opposite to the ground, 410px tall, sitting on the grid like any other frame with the same gaps on all sides. Inside it, top-left aligned on 24px padding: the wordmark at 28px, one sentence at 20px on up to three lines, the single action as a filled rectangle, and three text links on one line at the panel's foot.
hero.mobile: The text panel spans the full width as the first block, about 40% of the screen height, with the wordmark at 7vw, the sentence at 17px and the action full width. Under it the sheet resumes in two columns with 8px gaps, the right column started 60px higher than the left, colour strips kept on every frame. The links sit in one row at the panel's foot.
hero.headline: The wordmark at 28px plus one sentence of up to 70 characters inside the panel; nothing is set at display size.

motion.name: Shutter image
motion.description: The one hero or showcase image opens from an edge with a clip-path over about 1.1 seconds while the picture inside settles from 1.12 scale to rest. Use it once, on the image that matters most; later images simply are there. Recipe: 'Image shutter' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Accordion of tinted panels
sections.blueprint: A two-column introduction, then one horizontal accordion. Introduction: the heading, two to four words at clamp(36px, 4vw, 60px), in columns 1–5; one paragraph at 18px in columns 7–11. 64px below, a flex row across columns 1–12, 520px tall, of four to six panels with no gaps. The open stage is a panel taking about 58% of the width; the rest are vertical slivers sharing what remains. Order is carried by colour: the first stage is the darkest tone of one hue and each later stage is a lighter flat tint of it, so the row reads dark to light from left to right. A sliver shows only its stage name, rotated 90 degrees and reading upward, at 20px bold, anchored to its bottom-left. The open panel shows the name at 40px top-left, a 36ch paragraph at 18px bottom-left and, optionally, one photograph in its right half. Clicking a sliver opens it (flex-basis transition, 450ms).
sections.mobile: The accordion turns vertical: stages stack at full width as bars 64px tall in the same dark-to-light order, names set horizontally at 18px. The open stage expands to its content height with the paragraph at 17px. The first stage is open by default.

sections.name: Statement cell, dark rows
sections.blueprint: Two halves butted together, each 50vw wide and at least 90svh tall, with no gap. Left half, in a pale tone: the heading in three short lines at clamp(36px, 4.2vw, 68px), its middle line pushed flush right while the first and third stay flush left (text-align set per line), so the block zigzags inside the cell. A two-sentence paragraph of 30ch sits at the bottom-left and the single action at the bottom-right on the same baseline. Right half, in the darkest tone: four or five rows of equal height filling it, told apart by alternating two near-black tones, not by lines. Each row is a three-part grid: a title at 28px (5 parts), a short paragraph at 16px (4 parts) and a plain list of three terms at 15px (3 parts), all top-aligned with 28px padding. No images anywhere in the section.
sections.mobile: The halves stack. The light cell comes first at 70svh with the zigzag heading at 10vw and the paragraph at its foot. The dark rows follow at full width; each row stacks its title and paragraph, and its three terms run inline as one sentence separated by commas. Rows keep the alternating tones.

sections.name: Large marks on tiles
sections.blueprint: A board of filled tiles, four across and two or three rows deep, with 8px gaps, spanning the full content width. Each tile is about 3:2, one step lighter or darker than the page ground, with no border. A tile holds one supplied logo, shown far larger than a usual logo strip: about 72px tall, centred, in the page ink as a single-colour SVG. When no logo files exist, the tile holds the name instead, set at 28–32px bold, top-left with 24px padding; never draw a mark. One tile, twice the width of the others and placed first, is in the accent colour and carries the heading: two to four words at about 3vw, top-left. Tile corners follow the page's one radius, or the page's motif shape if it has one. Tiles sit still; there is no hover lift.
sections.mobile: Two tiles per row with 6px gaps, logos at 44px tall. The heading tile runs full width first, about 120px tall. Show eight tiles at most so the board stays under one and a half screens. Names set in type drop to 20px.

sections.name: One image across tiles
sections.blueprint: One photograph is cut across a board of tiles. A grid of six columns and four rows with 8px gaps spans the full width between 12px margins; every tile is square (aspect-ratio: 1). Each tile shows its own piece of the same image: set the photograph as every tile's background at background-size: 600% 400% and step background-position by column and row, so the picture reads whole through the gaps. Five of the twenty-four tiles are swapped for flat colour tiles from the palette, never two adjacent: one holds the heading (two to four words at 2.6vw, top-left, 16px padding), three hold one fact each at 18px, one holds the action. On hover a tile's piece scales to 108% inside its own clip. Choose a photograph with one clear subject, so the board is legible at a glance.
sections.mobile: Three columns by six rows with 6px gaps, the photograph re-cut at background-size 300% 600% from a portrait crop. Four colour tiles only; the heading tile spans two columns in the top row with the heading at 6vw. Facts drop to 15px.

sections.name: Photo strip, three-cell bar
sections.blueprint: A saturated flat field about 80svh tall. Across the top, 48px from the section edge, a strip of small photographs runs off both sides: all 150px tall at differing widths (3:4, 1:1, 3:2 in turn), 8px gaps, ten or more, drifting slowly as a marquee. A heading of two to four words at clamp(36px, 4vw, 60px) sits 72px below the strip at the left margin. 40px below the heading, the newsletter or booking form is one bar spanning the content width, 96px tall, divided into three equal cells with 8px gaps. Each cell is a filled block in a tone one step from the field with one radius: the first two are inputs (name, email) with placeholder text centred at 18px, the third is the submit action in the inverse colours with its word centred. Focus changes a cell's fill to the lightest tone. Small print at 13px sits under the first and third cells.
sections.mobile: The strip is 110px tall and scrolls by touch. The heading follows at 9vw. The three cells stack as full-width filled blocks 60px tall with 8px gaps, the submit block last. Small print sits beneath the stack, left-aligned.

references.name: Justin Lerner
references.idea: The portfolio is a hairline grid of square cells in which the letters of the owner's name are scattered among small animated project emblems, so name and work form one crossword-like board.
references.hero: White page divided by pale grey hairlines into five columns of exact squares (each 20vw), so three full rows and a sliver of a fourth show. No header, navigation or text block. Each cell holds one centred object about half the cell wide: either a single black slab-serif capital at 5.6vw (one in the top-left cell, one top-right, three more scattered through rows two and three) or a small project emblem such as a pixel speech bubble, a photographed bowl, a red robot arm, a wireframe figure, a logo badge or a line-drawn building. One cell holds only a soft blurred cloud. About 90% of the area is white.
references.type: Museo Slab is the only face on desktop: weight-500 capitals at 80px used as grid letters, with no body copy at all (eleven words on the page). Mobile adds light italic slab project names and small sans year tabs.
references.colour: #ffffff #e9eae8 #111111 #fff200 #f0563a #4fd0c8 — White ground, grey hairlines, black letters. Colour arrives only in the emblems, each in its own one- or two-colour scheme (yellow, coral, teal, purple). Mobile adds two solid yellow icon tiles.
references.imagery: Small spot illustrations and logos in deliberately mixed styles (pixel art, line drawing, isometric, wireframe mesh, one cut-out photo), each centred in a square cell with no frame or background, and animated.
references.layout: A single edge-to-edge grid of 20vw squares with hairline dividers and no outer margin; the whole site is about 1.3 screens. Mobile switches to two columns and adds a year tab in each cell's top-right corner and an italic name under each emblem.

sections.description: The grid continues for one more row below the fold with five cells holding only emblems. Across frames the emblems are caught in different states: a logo badge collapsing to a small monogram, a scan line moving down the wireframe figure, a pencil travelling across a drawn face, a coin appearing and disappearing. Each cell is a tiny looping or hover-driven animation, with no captions on desktop.

Mobile header built from the same cells: a small square with the initial on crosshair lines at left, an empty cell, then two solid-yellow square tiles carrying a document icon and a paper-plane icon. Below, the two-column grid gives each project a boxed year tab notched into the top-right corner of its cell and an italic slab project name near the bottom, sometimes overlapping the emblem.

steal: Spell the name by dropping its letters into scattered cells of a hairline grid and fill the remaining cells with project marks, so identity and index share one structure.
Give each project a single small animated emblem centred in a large empty square instead of a screenshot thumbnail.
On mobile, notch a small boxed year tab into the corner of each grid cell and label the cell with an italic name at its base.

references.name: Aspen Search
references.idea: The page is a ruled tile system with no margins: the two-word name is split across cells that alternate type, dithered canvas, black and one mint green.
references.hero: A 60px top bar ruled into cells: black logo square, local time, nav links starting at the centre line, a theme toggle and a black contact cell flush right. Below, the viewport is a two-by-two grid divided by 1px black lines, no outer margin. Top-left is white with the first word of the name at 12.5vw, weight 450, sitting bottom-left. Top-right and bottom-left cells hold a black-and-white dithered canvas crossed by large pale-grey blade shapes that ignore cell borders. The bottom-right quadrant splits into a black cell (24px white summary, mono caps action row at its base) and a mint cell (second statement, client-logo marquee along the bottom).
references.type: Suisse Intl at weight 450 for everything, tracking about -0.02em; Suisse Intl Mono in small caps for actions, bullet lists and footer. Wordmark 180px against 24px statements and 16px body. Later headings switch to all caps at about 9vw with leading near 0.9.
references.colour: #ffffff #232323 #d9d9d9 #a1ffcb #969797 — White, near-black and two greys fill the cells; a single mint green floods whole tiles (a statement, a stat, the closing call to action) as the only colour. Cool and flat.
references.imagery: A canvas of 1-bit ordered-dither dots with soft tonal blobs, overlaid with flat pale-grey shards taken from the logo; services get white wireframe line drawings of spheres. No photography anywhere.
references.layout: Zero page margin: everything is edge-to-edge cells on a two-column grid with halves subdivided, separated by 1px rules. Sections differ only by cell fill and cell height. Type always sits top-left or bottom-left in its cell with about 20px padding; some cells are left deliberately empty.

sections.description: The second screen continues the hero grid: a black cell carries a two-line all-caps slogan at about 9vw set hard against its left edge; a light grey cell top-right holds the second word of the name at the same giant size as the first, bottom-aligned; dither canvas fills the rest. Then a white row where the left half is empty and a 24px long-form text runs only in the right column.

Stair-stepped tiles instead of a row. A tall mint cell fills the left half with one figure at about 5vw in its top-left corner and nothing else. On the right, a shorter black tile starts higher with a white figure top-left and a small caption at its bottom edge; a grey tile sits to its right, stepped down, same internal layout. The tiles' unequal heights leave white notches.

Left half: a light grey cell with a three-line all-caps heading whose middle line is pushed to the right edge, a small paragraph low in the cell and a black mono-caps button bottom-right. Right half: black, split by hairlines into stacked rows; each row has a tiny mono index, a 28px title, a short paragraph in a second column, a white wireframe drawing and a mono caps list with small mint square bullets.

A grid of cells: white cell with a short statement top-left; a cell with a plain nav list; a cell with two small analogue clock icons and city times; a hairline row with email left and a social link right. Below, a black cell with the logo and lowercase wordmark centred large, beside a mint cell with a heading top-left and a thin diagonal arrow drawn into its bottom-right corner.

steal: Rule the whole viewport into cells with 1px lines and no page margin, then give the nav, the headline, the summary and the proof each its own cell with a flat fill.
Split a two-word brand name across two cells on consecutive screens at the same giant size, so scrolling completes the name.
Use a 1-bit ordered-dither texture as the picture in otherwise empty cells and let large flat logo fragments cross the cell borders to tie the grid together.
references.media: One halftone canvas of the brand mark is seen only through chosen cells of the tile grid, about half the hero area, and returns in sticky half panels and as a full-bleed canvas behind knockout words. Portraits are high-key black and white in a staggered row with offset heights, client logos keep their brand colours inside their own tiles, and there is no video and no rounded corner anywhere.
references.motion: A dark screen gives way at about 1.2s to a small mark on a 20s coin spin, the white grid arrives by 2.5s with the name rising through a mask, and the dither resolves by 4.5s. Lenis drives CSS sticky stacking (12 sticky elements, no pins): hero rows slide over each other and stat tiles lock under the header one by one; text fades in by line over 1000ms cubic-bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1) in 100ms steps (193 WAAPI calls), and a theme toggle wipes the page with a 1.2s clip-path sweep.

references.name: PP Neue Montreal
references.idea: A typeface specimen dressed as a vintage city travel guide: the font named after Montreal is sold through guidebook titling, postcards and old tourist footage.
references.hero: Grainy coral-red field. Top row: a monogram in a pale pill at left, a pale-grey pill nav with seven links centred, a black pill button at right. Below at the left margin, a two-line white bold title at about 4.5vw; opposite it, a ring of repeated monograms set around a circle like a stamp. Three full-width black hairlines cut the field into bands: a two-line intro sentence at ~1.6vw sits in the second, and the typeface name fills the third in black bold at ~17vw, two lines, tight leading, 60% of the width. A 4:3 clip of 1960s street footage is inset bottom-right, 29% wide, bottom-aligned with the name.
references.type: PP Neue Montreal only: Bold for display with -0.01em tracking and leading near 0.9, Text Regular 16px for body and lists. Sizes leap from 16px to 144px headings to a ~240px name; one section enlarges a single lowercase letter to viewport height.
references.colour: #ed4b44 #1a1a1a #f0e7d4 #18bc42 #b5b5b5 #f2c21a — Each chapter takes a flat field (coral red, near-black, cream, green) with black or cream type; one headline colours every word differently. Warm, print-poster feel with visible grain.
references.imagery: Archive 1960s city footage, saturated vintage postcards, a handwritten postcard back, and rotated specimen posters and stamp sheets scattered around a headline. All square-cornered and inset, never full-bleed.
references.layout: 24px side margins and full-width hairlines marking bands. Content is left-anchored in three or four columns split by vertical hairlines; chapters alternate between tabular lists, a scattered collage, a centred statement and a giant glyph comparison. A pill nav stays pinned.

sections.description: Near-black screen split by a vertical hairline at about 75% width. Left: a three-line small heading at the top margin, then a five-line bold oblique headline at ~6vw in which each line is indented further right like a staircase and each word takes its own colour (green, cream, grey, yellow, blue, orange). Right narrow column: two stacked postcards, one saturated photo card and one cream handwritten card with a stamp. A tiny section label sits bottom-left.

A dark band of pure tabular type. A body paragraph occupies column one; weight names stack as tight single-line lists in two further columns divided by vertical hairlines. Below, a small label over a full-width rule introduces a two-column timeline: years stacked at the left margin, release notes stacked from the centre line behind a short vertical rule. One text size, leading near 1.0, no decoration at all.

Dark full-viewport stage with a three-line cream headline at ~4vw placed dead centre. Around it eight or nine specimen artefacts (a stamp sheet, a green poster with a blue numeral, a grey flag chart, a rainbow ticket grid, concentric colour squares) are each rotated 10 to 30 degrees and arranged on a loose ring, several cropped by the viewport edge, as if tossed on a table.

Cream field. A caption row at the top: a two-line label at the left margin and a five-line paragraph starting at about 55% width. Then a full-width rule carrying a tiny label at each end naming the two cuts. Below it, two black lowercase letters, each roughly half the viewport wide and cropped by the bottom edge, one from each cut, so the reader compares shapes at poster scale.

steal: Give a product page a borrowed genre (here a tourist guidebook) and let that genre dictate titles, imagery and chapter names.
Cut a flat colour hero into bands with full-width hairlines and set the name at ~17vw in the bottom band beside a small inset film clip.
Scatter rotated print artefacts on a loose ring around a centred headline and let several crop off the viewport.
references.media: The hero is a red printed cover with paper grain; the real media is small, a 418x316 looping 1960s street clip at the bottom right (about 10% of the viewport) beside a wordmark filling about 60% of the width. Later: a postcard pair in the right half of a split, rotated ephemera orbiting a centred statement, full-bleed photo panels that slide up over the previous chapter, a spine accordion, and a full-bleed vintage photograph overscanned 72px each side; square corners, one video.
references.motion: Black, then a turning seal of logo letters, then the cover by 4.5s; four hero groups rise 25px and fade over 400ms cubic-bezier(0.44,0,0.56,1) at 200ms steps, settling at about 5.5s though the page loaded in 2.5s. Lenis drives a chain of sticky full-screen chapters: ephemera fly off as a photo panel slides up, a headline steps through weights of the variable cut on scroll, and a single glyph rotates and zooms for about 5 screens; about 390 appear fades run over 400ms on a spring-shaped linear() curve, with no reduced-motion rule.
